briefs.title: review list aggregate consistency testing
briefs.description: Use review list aggregate consistency testing to detect count and average values that describe a different snapshot from the returned reviews.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you detect a review list and its total or average describing different snapshots when they come from separate queries?

outline.heading: What Must Review List Aggregate Consistency Testing Detect?
outline.coverage: Define response invariants between review rows, totalReviews, and averageRating when the endpoint executes two database statements.

outline.heading: How Do You Detect a Review Count List Mismatch?
outline.coverage: Assert totalReviews equals the relevant returned rows for an unpaginated response and account for rows excluded by the user inner join.

outline.heading: What Is an Aggregate Snapshot Consistency Test?
outline.coverage: Coordinate a write between the list query and aggregate query and verify whether one response can combine different committed states.

outline.heading: Concurrent Review GET Race Scenarios
outline.coverage: Cover insert, update, and delete timing around both reads, with barriers that make the race deterministic rather than probabilistic.

outline.heading: How Does Postgres Separate Query Consistency Behave?
outline.coverage: Explain statement snapshots under the configured isolation assumptions and why a transaction may be needed for one-response consistency.

outline.heading: Average Rating Stale Response Detection
outline.coverage: Recalculate the expected average from returned ratings and identify legitimate differences versus snapshot drift.

outline.heading: Interleaving, List State, and Aggregate State Matrix
outline.coverage: Present deterministic write timing and the list, count, average, invariant, and expected test outcome.

outline.heading: How Do You Run a Deterministic Consistency Procedure?
outline.coverage: Use query barriers or transaction hooks to place one write between reads, assert the response invariant, and repeat under a chosen isolation level.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about snapshots, inner joins, transaction isolation, pagination assumptions, stale averages, and retrying reads.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: State the response-level invariant and direct readers to database and API testing skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test list and aggregate snapshot consistency
steps: Seed reviews with a known count and calculable average.
Install a deterministic barrier after the list query completes.
Insert, update, or delete a review while the request waits.
Release the aggregate query and capture the combined response.
Compare totalReviews with list length and recalculate the average.
Repeat inside a transaction using the intended isolation level.

codeExamples.focus: Insert, update, and delete review rows with known ratings while the GET request is paused.

briefs.title: skill content fallback outage testing
briefs.description: Use skill content fallback outage testing to prove playwright-cli remains downloadable while other skills preserve correct 404 and 500 responses.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you prove playwright-cli content remains downloadable on a database miss or exception while other skills retain 404 or 500 semantics?

outline.heading: What Must Skill Content Fallback Outage Testing Prove?
outline.coverage: Define the narrowly scoped playwright-cli fallback for both empty query results and caught failures, plus normal semantics for every other ID.

outline.heading: How Do You Write a Playwright-CLI Content Fallback Test?
outline.coverage: Mock the database to miss and throw, then assert status, markdown content type, and nonempty local SKILL.md output.

outline.heading: What Happens to a Database Outage Skill Download?
outline.coverage: Compare playwright-cli and an arbitrary skill slug when the select query rejects, without treating all skills as locally recoverable.

outline.heading: Content API Fallback Matrix
outline.coverage: Cover database hit, miss, exception, fallback file success, fallback file absence, UUID input, and unrelated slug input.

outline.heading: How Do You Run a 404 Versus 500 Download Test?
outline.coverage: Assert a clean miss returns 404 for other skills while a database exception returns 500, each with the expected JSON error.

outline.heading: Local Seed Markdown Availability
outline.coverage: Trace the fallback helper to the seeded playwright-cli content and test exact availability rather than substituting fixture text.

outline.heading: Database State, Skill ID, and Response Matrix
outline.coverage: Present the status, content type, body source, and fallback decision for every supported branch.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Outage Simulation Procedure?
outline.coverage: Execute hit, miss, and exception cases with isolated mocks, then validate the real fallback file in a repository integration test.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about why one skill has a fallback, UUID behavior, content type, seed files, 404 versus 500, and artifact route differences.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Summarize the narrow recovery contract and link to the playwright-cli skill.

procedurePlan.heading: How to verify content fallback behavior
steps: Assert the real playwright-cli fallback markdown can be read from the repository.
Mock a database hit and verify canonical generated markdown wins.
Mock an empty result for playwright-cli and assert the local markdown response.
Mock a thrown query for playwright-cli and assert the same fallback response.
Repeat miss and exception cases with an unrelated slug.
Assert exact 404 and 500 JSON semantics for the unrelated slug.

codeExamples.title: Read the real local playwright-cli markdown
codeExamples.focus: Assert the fallback helper resolves and returns the seeded SKILL.md rather than test-only text.

briefs.title: trending leaderboard recency tie testing
briefs.description: Use trending leaderboard recency tie testing to prove newer skills win equal weekly-install counts and expose unresolved timestamp ties in CI.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you prove newer skills win weekly-install ties and identify residual ties when createdAt is also equal?

outline.heading: What Must Trending Leaderboard Recency Tie Testing Prove?
outline.coverage: Define weeklyInstalls as the primary key, createdAt descending as the secondary key, and the residual nondeterminism when both values match.

outline.heading: How Does the Weekly Installs Recency Tiebreaker Work?
outline.coverage: Seed equal weekly counts with distinct timestamps and assert the newer record receives the lower rank number.

outline.heading: What Is a Trending Rank Same Count Test?
outline.coverage: Use three or more tied rows to prove ordering is based on recency rather than insertion sequence or UUID.

outline.heading: CreatedAt Secondary Sort QA
outline.coverage: Test timezone-equivalent timestamps, millisecond differences, and identical timestamp fixtures against descending order.

outline.heading: How Do You Assert New Skill Trending Order?
outline.coverage: Compare trending with all, hot, and new filters so the recency rule is asserted only where the route defines it.

outline.heading: Leaderboard Residual Tie Test
outline.coverage: Repeat requests for rows tied on both fields and document the need for a unique final tiebreaker without claiming one exists.

outline.heading: Weekly Counts, Timestamps, and Expected Ranks
outline.coverage: Present fixtures and expected order for unique counts, recency ties, exact ties, and the top-50 boundary.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Ranking Procedure?
outline.coverage: Seed timestamp-controlled rows, clear the filter-specific cache, request trending, and assert ordered IDs and contiguous ranks.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about descending order, cache effects, timestamp precision, exact ties, filter differences, and deterministic SQL.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Summarize the documented and residual tie behavior and link to leaderboard testing skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test trending tie order
steps: Seed skills with controlled weeklyInstalls and createdAt combinations.
Delete the leaderboard:trending cache key before each assertion.
Request the trending leaderboard and collect returned IDs and ranks.
Assert higher weekly counts sort first.
Assert newer timestamps sort first when weekly counts tie.
Repeat exact ties and record whether a unique final tiebreaker is needed.

codeExamples.focus: Exercise weeklyInstalls descending followed by createdAt descending and rank assignment.

codeExamples.focus: Create fixtures that isolate primary, secondary, and residual tie behavior.

briefs.title: Postgres pagination count consistency
briefs.description: Use Postgres pagination count consistency tests to expose page rows and total counts taken from different snapshots during concurrent writes.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you detect inconsistent total counts when the page query and count query run in parallel during concurrent writes?

outline.heading: What Must Postgres Pagination Count Consistency Prove?
outline.coverage: Define invariants among returned rows, total, page, limit, and totalPages while acknowledging that two statements may observe different commits.

outline.heading: How Do You Reproduce a Parallel Count Query Race?
outline.coverage: Pause the page and count branches independently and insert or delete matching rows between their snapshots.

outline.heading: What Is a Pagination Total Mismatch Test?
outline.coverage: Assert total is compatible with the page contents, offset, and limit, especially on the final page and after concurrent changes.

outline.heading: Postgres Snapshot Consistency API Choices
outline.coverage: Compare current Promise.all statements with a transaction snapshot and a single window-count query as testable designs.

outline.heading: How Do You Test the Drizzle Count and Rows Query?
outline.coverage: Verify both branches receive identical where conditions and that count conversion and totalPages calculations are correct.

outline.heading: Concurrent Insert Pagination Drift Cases
outline.coverage: Use matching and nonmatching inserts, deletes, and updates around first, middle, and final pages.

outline.heading: Interleaving, Page Length, Total, and TotalPages Matrix
outline.coverage: Present controlled write timing and exact response expectations for each pagination state.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Count Consistency Procedure?
outline.coverage: Create enough rows for multiple pages, coordinate query barriers, mutate data, and validate response arithmetic and snapshot assumptions.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about Promise.all, statement snapshots, window counts, final-page invariants, deterministic order, and transaction cost.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: State the pagination consistency oracle and direct readers to database skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test page and count consistency
steps: Seed at least three pages of skills matching one filter.
Place independent barriers around the rows and count queries.
Start the API request and release one query first.
Insert, delete, or update one matching row before releasing the other query.
Assert rows, total, and totalPages against the chosen snapshot contract.
Repeat inside a transaction or with a single-query alternative for comparison.

codeExamples.focus: Insert and mutate rows that do and do not match the active filter.

briefs.title: unknown category type handling testing
briefs.description: Use unknown category type handling testing to detect taxonomy rows silently omitted when unrestricted database values miss four API groups early.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you detect category rows silently omitted because their unrestricted type does not match one of four response groups?

outline.heading: What Must Unknown Category Type Handling Testing Detect?
outline.coverage: Define the four recognized group keys and show how an unrestricted text value can be skipped without an error.

outline.heading: How Do You Write an Invalid Category Type Test?
outline.coverage: Insert a uniquely named category with an unsupported type, call the endpoint, and assert the omission is visible to the test oracle.

outline.heading: What Causes Silent Taxonomy Row Omission?
outline.coverage: Trace the grouped[row.type] guard and explain why the loop neither returns the row nor reports an invalid type.

outline.heading: Category Enum Constraint Testing Options
outline.coverage: Compare a PostgreSQL check constraint, enum, application validation, and explicit unknown group as alternative contracts.

outline.heading: How Do You Run Unknown Grouping Key QA?
outline.coverage: Use empty, case-variant, whitespace, typo, and future category types to expose silent data loss.

outline.heading: Database API Completeness Check
outline.coverage: Compare the count and IDs from the category table with the union of response arrays, then report omitted IDs.

outline.heading: Stored Types, Response Groups, and Outcomes
outline.coverage: Present recognized and unsupported values with group destination, inclusion status, and recommended assertion.

outline.heading: How Do You Implement the Completeness Procedure?
outline.coverage: Seed one row per valid type plus invalid controls, clear the categories cache, call GET, and compare database and response ID sets.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about text columns, enums, forward compatibility, cache invalidation, omissions, and API schema stability.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: State the completeness invariant and link to taxonomy and database testing resources.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test unknown category types
steps: Seed one category for each recognized type and two unsupported controls.
Delete the categories:all cache key.
Call the categories endpoint and collect every returned category ID.
Query all seeded category IDs directly from PostgreSQL.
Compare both sets and identify omitted unsupported rows.
Add the chosen schema or API control and rerun the completeness assertion.
